title: dj-migrations-panel
summary: A visual representation of your migrations along with a snapshot of what models were changed and what SQL was was/will be executed by a migration.
rationale: Similar to urls or signal inspecting panels, it is useful to have this level of application information in one easily searchable place.
author: yassi

title: django-huey support
summary: Support for huey for managing workers and tasks, similar to what is available in dj-celery-panel
rationale: It would add support for managing another popular task system through the admin.
author: Natgho

title: orm queries execution panel
summary: We want a usecase where from admin panel dev users with staff role can execute all read only like orm queries and see the results, like manage.py dbshell equivalent using django orm style. most server cli shell utlitities like kubectx etc would need prod cluster access which devops team don't usually provide to dev teams.
rationale: Devs often need to run custom queries to debug production issues or gather evidence for new features that they might be developing/working on. Asking devops teams or owner teams with this info creates dependency and is a major blocker for developers and creates friction in product development.
author: utkarshpandey12

title: django guardian support
summary: a monitoring tool that could trigger the operations listed in the cheat sheet from the admin panel, along with assigned permissions, revoked permissions, permission changes, current permission tables and their sizes, I'm sure it would be perfect.
rationale: Better observability for guardian operations and extra functionality.
author: Natgho

title: dj-command-panel
summary: Expose a Django project's management commands and information about them. Allow a user to run commands from the admin.
rationale: This is both useful as a way to quickly inspect what commands are available and as a way to execute commands quickly through the admin. There are quite a few issues to figure out such as where commands will execute and how to make sure the running web processes are unaffected.
author: yassi

title: pip freeze panel
summary: Ability to inspect the python environment and the installed packages and metadata. A similar package is built in one of the DCR tutorials - this wishlist item calls for a more fleshed out solution.
rationale: This is useful for quickly checking what's available in the current environment and looking up information (docs, etc.) In production, a coding agent may not have access to your python environment but may have access to this DCR tool via MCP to provide context about the python environment.
author: yassi

title: s3 panel
summary: Tool for browsing s3 buckets via the Django admin.
rationale: Decrease the need to leave the Django admin to perform a basic task like looking up a file or image in the AWS s3 browser UI.
author: yassi

title: dj-storage-panel
summary: Browse configured storage backends, list buckets and files, and spot orphaned uploads.
rationale: Media files drift from database records and nobody notices for months.
author: yassi

title: dj-migrations-panel
summary: See migration state, history. ability to rollback to specific migration (Danger!) and the ability to author manual migration files when needed.
rationale: Deploys go wrong when nobody knows which migrations already ran on staging versus production. Also sometimes developers need to make their own migration files, there is space for a tool that could facilitate that.
author: yassi

title: dj-mail-panel
summary: Inspect outgoing email: rendered previews, delivery attempts, bounces, and a replay button.
rationale: Debugging transactional email currently means digging through provider dashboards.
author: yassi

title: dj-settings-panel
summary: Introspection for settings through the admin. Possibly add ways to change settings live (needs discussion)
rationale: Facilitate looking up settings without having to look through a possibly very large settings file.
author: yassi
